cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Every systematic review begins with a perfectly reasonable request.

cues.speaker: PI
cues.text: Just a quick review. Shouldn't take long.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Then the abstracts arrive. The search was comprehensive. Unfortunately, so were the consequences. Welcome to Club Eligibility. Full text upstairs.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: The generative model arrives with an entourage, a limousine, and the ability to turn one screening decision into a TED Talk.

cues.speaker: LLM
cues.text: Before deciding whether to retain this abstract, we must consider the epistemological status of relevance.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: You've written more about whether to read the abstract than the authors wrote in the abstract.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Jev arrives with a folding stool. Jev does decisions.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Give this zero-shot classifier the title, abstract, and eligibility criteria. It returns a structured decision with probabilities. No bespoke training. No free-text monologue. Here, one question orders the queue for human screening.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Eight diagnostic test accuracy reviews. Twenty-six thousand, eight hundred and thirty-two records with abstracts. Mean WSS at ninety-five: zero point six six one.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: That's work saved over sampling at ninety-five percent recall, measured retrospectively. It isn't accuracy. Performance varies by review. The article reports a bill of about one dollar forty-six.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: Finally, research infrastructure we can expense without forming a steering committee.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: The published three-model ensemble does better: zero point six eight zero. Add embedding reranking: zero point seven zero eight. Jev remains impressively competitive for something with less furniture.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: Three models, one decision. A committee meeting with measurable output. Unsettling. Please record this unprecedented event in the minutes.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: These are published benchmark comparisons, using older models. Today's competitors may change the picture.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Management spots an opportunity for improvement. Replace the single overall question with five criterion questionnaires. Five times the judgements. Surely that means better screening?

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: In this tested setup, the probability-based expected-score variant reaches only zero point five three six. More machinery. Worse ranking.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: We added bureaucracy and performance got worse. Finally, AI understands academia.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: The questions or scoring might be the problem. That's a hypothesis. Decomposition hasn't been convicted.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: One question. How do you know when to stop screening?

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: The evaluator consults the known benchmark labels. Those labels locate the ninety-five percent recall point after scoring. Jev never sees them. A retrospective result doesn't give a new review a validated stopping rule.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: Excellent crystal ball. Does it work before we know which studies are relevant? My protocol has a surprisingly strict policy on clairvoyance.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Before trusting automated exclusions, prospectively validate thresholds, calibration, and stopping rules. Test other review types too. A probability needs checking, and eight DTA reviews aren't the whole evidence-synthesis universe.

cues.speaker: Paper
cues.text: The methods are in the full text.

cues.speaker: Librarian
cues.text: Of course they are. Heaven forbid the abstract become useful.

cues.speaker: Narrator
cues.text: Jev works the queue. The librarian keeps the keys. Cheap decisions. Expensive questions.
